blocks: ## Ownership Is Everywhere in Real Communication
Possessive endings allow you to speak efficiently about people and the things connected to them. They are essential for personal information, family, home, school, travel and everyday descriptions.
The ending carries the meaning of the owner.
- اِسْمِي لَيْلَى. — My name is Layla.
- هَذَا بَيْتُنَا. — This is our house.
- أَيْنَ حَقِيبَتُكَ؟ — Where is your bag?
- مَدْرَسَتُهَا كَبِيرَةٌ. — Her school is large.
[callout] Curriculum connection Possessive endings help you identify relationships and ownership in listening and reading, answer personal questions in speaking and add precision to writing.
## Use the chapter at the depth you need
Revise the Core route first, then continue into Develop and Stretch when you are ready. You do not need to complete the whole chapter in one sitting.
- Match each suffix to its owner.
- Recognise every possessive suffix attached to a noun.
- Connect each subject pronoun to its possessive ending.
- Attach suffixes to regular nouns accurately.
- Change ة to ت before a suffix.
- Use possessive nouns in complete sentences.
- Maintain accurate noun and adjective agreement.
- Apply the forms in reading, speaking and writing.
- I can transform كِتَاب into “my, your, his, her and their book”.
- I can distinguish ـكَ from ـكِ .
- I can distinguish ـكُمْ from ـكُنَّ .
- I can write مَدْرَسَتِي , not مَدْرَسَةِي .
- I can explain why a possessed noun does not take الـ .
Possessive endings grow from the subject-pronoun family learned in Lesson 1.
## From an Independent Pronoun to an Attached Ending
The owner is not written as a separate subject pronoun after the noun. Instead, a short ending is attached directly to the noun.
[callout] Do not translate word by word English uses a separate possessive word: my book . Arabic builds one grammatical unit: كِتَابِي . The ending cannot stand alone.
Choose a noun and an owner. The correct Arabic form will appear.
[callout] Preview of later grammar The same attached-pronoun family will later appear with verbs and prepositions. In this lesson, focus only on ownership attached to nouns.
### Game 1: Match the Ending to Its Meaning
Select one Arabic ending and its English meaning.
Generate a noun and an owner. Build the correct possessive form before revealing the answer.

TABLE: Owner | Subject pronoun | Ending | Possessive form | Meaning // First singular | أَنَا | ـِي | كِتَابِي | my book // First plural | نَحْنُ | ـنَا | كِتَابُنَا | our book // Second masculine singular | أَنْتَ | ـكَ | كِتَابُكَ | your book // Second feminine singular | أَنْتِ | ـكِ | كِتَابُكِ | your book // Second dual | أَنْتُمَا | ـكُمَا | كِتَابُكُمَا | your book, two people // Second masculine/mixed plural | أَنْتُمْ | ـكُمْ | كِتَابُكُمْ | your book // Second feminine plural | أَنْتُنَّ | ـكُنَّ | كِتَابُكُنَّ | your book // Third masculine singular | هُوَ | ـهُ | كِتَابُهُ | his book // Third feminine singular | هِيَ | ـهَا | كِتَابُهَا | her book // Third dual | هُمَا | ـهُمَا | كِتَابُهُمَا | their book, two people // Third masculine/mixed plural | هُمْ | ـهُمْ | كِتَابُهُمْ | their book // Third feminine plural | هُنَّ | ـهُنَّ | كِتَابُهُنَّ | their book
[example] كِتَابُكَ your book — speaking to one male
[example] كِتَابُكِ your book — speaking to one female
The written consonants are the same. The final vowel carries the gender distinction.
[example] كِتَابُكُمْ / كِتَابُكُنَّ your book — male/mixed plural / female plural
[example] كِتَابُهُمْ / كِتَابُهُنَّ their book — male/mixed plural / female plural
Pronounce the doubled نّ clearly in feminine plural forms.
[callout] Pattern families Second-person endings begin with ك : ـكَ، ـكِ، ـكُمَا، ـكُمْ، ـكُنَّ . Third-person endings begin with ه : ـهُ، ـهَا، ـهُمَا، ـهُمْ، ـهُنَّ .
## Four Rules for Building Possessive Nouns
The suffix becomes part of the written word.
The possessive ending already makes the noun definite: a specific book belonging to someone.
Tanwīn and a possessive suffix do not remain together.
The hidden ت appears when another ending is attached.
### Pattern lab Nouns ending in ة

TABLE: Base noun | Meaning | With suffix | Meaning // مَدْرَسَةٌ | school | مَدْرَسَتِي | my school // حَقِيبَةٌ | bag | حَقِيبَتُكِ | your bag, feminine singular // غُرْفَةٌ | room | غُرْفَتُهُ | his room // سَيَّارَةٌ | car | سَيَّارَتُهَا | her car // أُسْرَةٌ | family | أُسْرَتُنَا | our family

[callout] Stretch: the short vowel before the suffix The short case vowel before a suffix may change according to the noun’s role in the sentence: هَذَا كِتَابُهُ but فِي كِتَابِهِ . The possessive ending still identifies the same owner. At this stage, secure the suffix first.

## Move from a Word to Meaningful Communication
### Pattern 1 This is my / your / his…
[example] هَذَا كِتَابِي. This is my book.
[example] هَذِهِ حَقِيبَتُكِ. This is your bag, speaking to one female.
[example] هَذَا بَيْتُنَا. This is our house.
[example] هَذِهِ سَيَّارَتُهُ. This is his car.
[example] أَيْنَ كِتَابُكَ؟ Where is your book? — one male
[example] أَيْنَ حَقِيبَتُكِ؟ Where is your bag? — one female
[example] هَلْ هَذَا فَصْلُكُمْ؟ Is this your classroom? — male or mixed group
[example] مَا اسْمُهَا؟ What is her name?
[example] كِتَابُهَا الْجَدِيدُ مُفِيدٌ. Her new book is useful.
[example] سَيَّارَتُهُ الْجَدِيدَةُ سَرِيعَةٌ. His new car is fast.
[callout] Agreement insight The adjective agrees with the thing possessed , not the owner. سَيَّارَتُهُ takes a feminine adjective because سَيَّارَة is feminine, although the owner is male.
Read for ownership. Underline each attached ending and identify its owner.

## Learn by playing with ownership and attachment
Each game strengthens a different decision: identify the owner, choose the suffix, attach it accurately, use it in context and repair mistakes.
Each preserved game now appears beside the language point it practises.
## Common Mistakes and How to Repair Them
Arabic normally attaches the possessive ending to the noun.
The suffix already makes the noun definite.
ة changes before an attached ending.
The adjective must describe the feminine noun سَيَّارَة .
The adjective agrees with the possessed object.
[callout] Repair strategy Separate the decision into two parts: What is the noun? Then ask: Who owns it? Attach only the ending that represents that owner.
- Match the twelve endings to meanings.
- Build possessive forms with كِتَاب and بَيْت .
- Practise ة ← ت with a visible model.
- Use possessive nouns in questions and answers.
- Track owners in a short reading text.
- Use dual and feminine plural endings accurately.
- Notice case-vowel changes before the same suffix.
- Write a connected paragraph with varied owners and precise reference.
